clue.text: Principal earnings

parts.note: read as 'main income' it suggests a salary, but it means the money earned on a principal sum lent or deposited at a bank

explanation.surface: A phrase that sounds like someone's chief source of income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principal' looks like an adjective meaning main; here it is the noun, the capital sum on which a lender or saver is paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank pays a percentage on the capital you deposit, and that percentage return is what a principal sum earns.

clue.text: Displeasure apparent about many turning up dirty

indicators.note: about means going round, so the anger word wraps the other letters

parts.note: displeasure that shows is anger, which crosswords give as ire
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a crossword stand-in for many

indicators.note: turning signals that the little word beside it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone visibly annoyed that a crowd has shown up looking filthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparent' just says the displeasure shows; 'many' as M is the Roman thousand, and 'turning' flips the little word 'up' before both go inside the anger word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something contaminated or unclean is impure, the opposite of pure.

clue.text: Having dash, around 50, and smart

indicators.note: around signals that the dash word is wrapped round the number

parts.note: a dash of colour is a slight tinge
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone stylish, energetic and about fifty years old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' looks like an adjective for the dashing fifty-year-old; it is the verb meaning to sting.
explanation.definitionFit: To smart is to feel a sharp stinging sensation, a prickling of the skin.

clue.text: Go on without one, patently amused

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the ranting word sits round the numeral

parts.note: to go on at length, haranguing, is to rant
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone told to carry on alone, clearly finding it funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is the old sense 'outside': RANT goes round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Riant is a literary word for laughing or cheerful, so visibly amused.

clue.text: Directions left with a boor to dispose of everything

parts.note: S and E are the compass points south and east
a lout is a rough, uncouth fellow

explanation.surface: Instructions given to an oaf for clearing out all the stock.
explanation.definitionFit: When a shop or event has no stock or tickets remaining, the whole lot has been sold.

clue.text: Herb for healing a lamb's affliction

indicators.note: an affliction troubles and upsets, so the letters beside it are disordered

explanation.surface: A herbal remedy recommended for a sick lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of A LAMBS, from 'a lamb's', are rearranged; 'affliction' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsam is a fragrant plant, and its resin is used in soothing ointments.

clue.text: Rates a page, then cracks up

parts.note: to crack someone up is to speak of them highly

explanation.surface: Someone grades a page of writing and then bursts out laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracks up' suggests laughing; it is the phrase meaning to extol, as in 'not all it's cracked up to be'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to judge its worth, as a valuer assesses a property.

clue.text: Readiest to adapt, as more stable

indicators.note: to adapt is to alter, so the letters of the word beside it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Those most prepared to change are the most balanced.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadier is the comparative of steady, meaning firmer and less liable to wobble.

clue.text: Fashion class that's not going to extremes

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or style
a rate is a grade or class, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: A style category that avoids anything too extreme.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderate describes keeping within reasonable limits, avoiding excess.

clue.text: Investing money in a boat which is tip-top

indicators.note: investing in its sense of clothing or enclosing, so the money is placed inside the boat

parts.note: a pinnace is a small boat carried by a ship
L stands for pound, the British unit of money

explanation.surface: Putting cash into a boat that is first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investing' suggests finance, but signals the money L going inside PINNACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Here tip-top is the noun, the very top or peak, as of a mountain or career.

clue.text: Wretched housing before getting extended

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so the sad word encloses the other

parts.note: wretched means sad or miserable
pre is the Latin prefix for before

explanation.surface: A miserable dwelling ahead of being made bigger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' looks like a noun for homes but is the verb of containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Spread out means stretched or extended over a wider area.

clue.text: Wine available in plastic dispensers

indicators.note: available in says the wine can be found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A wine sold from plastic dispensers.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from the Piedmont region of Italy.

clue.text: Lots are in unwonted liaison

indicators.note: unwonted means unusual or out of the ordinary, so the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Many people are caught up in an unusual love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a connection or dealings between parties, which this plural noun names.

clue.text: Collaborator writing excellent article in German

parts.note: excellent is A1, here written with the letter I standing for the figure one
der is the German masculine definite article

explanation.surface: A partner writing an excellent piece in German.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means first-rate; 'writing' tells you to write the 1 as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An aider is a helper or assistant, someone who works with another.

clue.text: Bitter sweet?

definitions.meaning: sharp or sour to the taste
a pastry dessert with a filling, a sweet course; the question mark flags the noun sense

explanation.definitionFit: Tart means acid in flavour, and a tart is a pastry pudding filled with fruit or jam.

clue.text: Getting badly beat means humiliation

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of the next words are put in a poor arrangement

explanation.surface: Losing heavily brings shame.
explanation.definitionFit: Abasement is the lowering of someone's dignity, a degrading loss of pride.

clue.text: Look over quiet to be admitted to trendy party

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing

indicators.note: being admitted means let inside, so the quiet letter enters the party word

parts.note: a sect is a faction or party
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Checking whether a quiet person may get into a fashionable party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' suggests a celebration, but here it is a faction, SECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine closely, scrutinising carefully.

clue.text: Spot-on bill a minister presented

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a curate is an assistant minister of the church

explanation.surface: A minister is handed a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means precisely correct, without error.

clue.text: A stretcher for use in the dark!

definitions.text: A stretcher for use in the dark!

parts.words: A stretcher for use in the dark!
parts.note: the stretcher suggests a medical litter; it is a photographic device in a darkroom that makes prints bigger

explanation.surface: A device for carrying the injured at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretcher' points to first aid; a darkroom device that magnifies a negative onto paper stretches the image.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographer uses this projector in a darkroom to make prints bigger than the negative.

clue.text: Hold on — it can explode!

indicators.note: exploding blows apart, so the letters of the words beside it are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning to wait because a can could blow up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold on' reads as a phrase meaning wait; only 'Hold' is the definition and 'on' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To contain is to hold within, as a jar holds jam.

clue.text: Call a guy up over a key

indicators.note: over in a down clue means placed on top of what follows
up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a guy is a man
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Phoning a man about a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses MAN to NAM; 'over' puts it above E in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To call someone something is to give them a title or label.

clue.text: Spots not considered

definitions.meaning: an outbreak of red marks on the skin

explanation.definitionFit: A rash is a skin eruption, and a rash act is reckless and ill-judged.

clue.text: Book having to do with verse-composition

parts.note: re means concerning or about, as in business letters

indicators.note: composition means putting together, so the letters of the word beside it are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A volume concerned with writing poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a noun for the volume of verse; it is the verb meaning to make a booking.
explanation.definitionFit: To book a table is to reserve it, holding it in advance.

clue.text: Joint holding as in a gambling organisation

indicators.note: holding means keeping inside, so the joint prefix wraps the two small words

parts.note: co- is the prefix meaning joint, as in co-owner
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dive that keeps its stake inside a betting firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like the slang for a dive or club; it is the prefix meaning joint, as in co-author and co-owner, holding the two small words.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a house where roulette, cards and other games of chance are played for money.

clue.text: Got together with a little work in the Mediterranean

indicators.note: in signals that the unit of work goes inside the sea

parts.note: the Med is the common short name for the Mediterranean
an erg is a tiny unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Joined up with some light work in the Mediterranean sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Merged means combined into one, as two companies unite.

clue.text: Practice America for example backs

parts.note: USA is the United States of America

indicators.note: backs here means goes backwards, so the abbreviation for example is reversed

parts.note: eg is short for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: The USA, for instance, supports a particular custom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' looks like 'supports'; it reverses EG to GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is habitual practice, the customary way of doing something.

clue.text: Crush the fellow framing a virtuous man in charge

indicators.note: framing means surrounding like a frame, so the fellow word goes round the rest

parts.note: a mate is a fellow or companion
ST is short for saint, a virtuous man

explanation.surface: A man stitching up a saintly boss to ruin him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'framing' suggests stitching up an innocent man, but it signals containment: the fellow word goes round the article, the saint and the in-charge abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To masticate is to chew, grinding food between the teeth.

clue.text: Taking in an egghead? Senseless!

indicators.note: taking means extracting, so the answer is drawn out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry at someone bringing in an intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like the word for an intellectual, but it only supplies its first letter to the run hidden across 'in an egghead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly and lacking sense or meaning.

clue.text: Crooked gang, having dropped leader, got ahead

indicators.note: dropping the leader means losing the first letter of the word beside it

parts.note: to have led is to have got ahead or been in front

explanation.surface: A bent gang that got in front after losing its boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked gang' reads as one phrase; 'Crooked' is the definition, meaning bent at an angle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something angled is set at a slant, bent away from the straight.

clue.text: Establishing credit, being a consumer

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
a consumer of food is eating

explanation.surface: Building a credit rating while spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumer' suggests a shopper; here it is someone consuming food.
explanation.definitionFit: Creating means bringing into being, founding or setting up.

clue.text: In time a little beast will make mistakes

indicators.note: in signals that the creature is placed inside the period word

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is a small animal

explanation.surface: A small creature will eventually go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are errors in a printed book, often listed on a slip of corrections.

clue.text: Place to get present for small daughter

parts.note: here means present, in attendance
taken as written
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Where to get a gift for a young girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' suggests a gift; it means in attendance. HEREFORD is an English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereford is a city in the west of England, a town on the river Wye.
